extracted.intended_audience: patent proprietors, prospective opponents, and patent attorneys considering or involved in European Patent (EPO) opposition proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on filing, defending and conducting oppositions to European patents at the EPO, including admissibility, grounds, procedural steps, amendment limits, costs, and appeals. Intended to help opponents, patentees and their representatives navigate the opposition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for filing an opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition must be filed within nine months of the official date of grant of the European patent, and the opposition fee must be paid by the same date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions are possible to the deadline for filing an opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any natural or legal person (other than the owner of the patent being opposed) may file an opposition to a granted European patent. More than one opposition may be filed against the same patent by more than one person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents may file jointly using a common representative or separately. A firm of patent attorneys can file in their own name to keep the identity of the opponent secret. The status as an opponent cannot be freely transferred — oppositions can only be transferred/assigned to a third party together with the business assets in the interests of which the opposition was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposition (limited grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition must include a statement of the grounds. The limited grounds on which a European patent can be opposed are: (1) that the subject-matter of the patent is not patentable (lacking novelty, inventive step, industrial application or relating to excluded subject-matter); (2) that the invention is not sufficiently described to allow a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention; (3) that the subject-matter of the patent extends beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When opposing a patent it is important to set out as full a case as possible at the outset, indicating all relevant facts, evidence and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to present and substantiate grounds at the outset
rubrics_metrics.description: If a ground of opposition is not mentioned and substantiated at the outset, it may not be possible to introduce it later during the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions must set out as full a case as possible initially; late introduction of unmentioned grounds is generally not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before substantive examination the opposition division examines whether the opposition has been validly filed (i.e., whether it is admissible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common reasons for inadmissibility include the fee not being paid on time, or the opponent not being unambiguously identified. Inadmissible oppositions are rejected (but forwarded to the proprietor for information) and the procedure ends with a (appealable) decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition division composition and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings are conducted before an opposition division which includes three technically qualified examiners, at least two of whom must have taken no part in the proceedings for grant of the patent. Sometimes a legally qualified examiner who took no part in grant may also take part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The composition ensures that members were not involved in grant where required, preserving impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural sequence and deadlines (written and oral phases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are initially conducted by written correspondence; they will end in an oral hearing if one is requested by a party. If the opposition is admissible, the patent proprietor is usually set a deadline (usually four months) for submitting arguments and amendments in response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After proprietor's reply the EPO issues a preliminary opinion inviting further comments; once comments are in (or deadlines expire) a hearing is usually scheduled if oral proceedings were requested. Specific timing steps are described in the guide (e.g., typical +1–4 months, +4 months, +2–4 months etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on amendments during opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Only amendments that respond directly to a ground of opposition are allowed. Added matter is not permitted; claim broadening is also not allowed, even if it would be necessary to address a ground of opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a feature present in claim 1 is alleged to add matter, it cannot be deleted in response if doing so would broaden scope of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent proprietor's obligation to reply and strategic advice
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no obligation on the patent proprietor to reply to the opponent’s arguments, but the EPO will examine the merits of every admissible opposition regardless of whether the proprietor replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit a response that strongly refutes the opponent’s arguments risks the EPO reaching a summary judgment in favour of the opponent. For this reason proprietors tend to respond as a matter of routine, even if the opponent’s case appears strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and argumentation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions should indicate all relevant facts, evidence and arguments supporting the stated grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most of the opponent’s cost is professional time preparing the notice of opposition and grounds; thorough initial preparation and evidence is important for admissibility and substantive assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation and limits on cost recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: To a large extent each side bears its own costs in opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apportionment of costs may be made by the opposition division only in certain limited circumstances (such as abuse of procedure), and only if requested before a final decision is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual renewal fees remain payable during opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual renewal fees are still payable on the individual granted national patents during an opposition process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is amended as a result of opposition, a procedure similar to that following a notice of allowance before grant is followed to implement the amendments in each designated state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical costs for opponents and proprietors (budgeting guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated typical costs and cost drivers are provided for preparing/filing a notice of opposition, reviewing patentee’s observations, preparing further submissions, preparing for oral proceedings, and attending oral proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: preparing & filing a notice: £4,000–£15,000 (typical £5,000); reviewing observations: £2,000–£5,000 (typical £3,000); further submissions: £4,000–£10,000; preparing for oral proceedings: £2,000–£10,000 (typical £5,000); attending oral proceedings: £3,000–£10,000 (typical £4,500). Overall typical total ~£10,000–£40,000 (typical £15,000–£20,000) over about 2 years. Proprietor defence costs are similar but with higher amounts for reviewing/responding and drafting fall-back positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals during opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party adversely affected by a decision may appeal. In situations where a patent is maintained in amended form, both parties are entitled to appeal against the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one party appeals (e.g., the opponent), the other party is automatically joined and entitled to respond. If the patentee is the non-appealing party, the patentee will not be permitted to make amendments to the claims during appeal that would put them in a better position than before the appeal was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability and expected duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings are contentious and inter partes; outcomes are often hard to predict and uncertainty about patent validity may persist until the decision is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not unusual for opposition proceedings to take over two years to conclude; appeals can extend uncertainty for a further two years or more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings attendance and publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings will occur if requested by a party; the patent proprietor(s) and other interested parties such as their attorney may be present but attendance is not compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral proceedings are typically one day; summons and timing steps precede oral proceedings, and preparatory written submissions may be filed in response to the opposition division's preliminary views.
